title: Retire the execution machinery: delete what ticfac now owns
description:
ticfac Phase 2 copied the execution machinery out of this repository behind a
clean, pinned, dependency-free boundary — and removed nothing. Until the
originals go, "extracted" means "copied", and two implementations drift.

This epic is planned HERE, in the tracker of the repository whose code it
deletes, and run by ticfac against this checkout (`ticfac run-epic <epic>
--repo ~/Development/ticks`). That is why it needs no cross-repo dispatch
machinery: the tracker lives with the code.

It is also the PRODUCTION run ticfac Phase 3 asks for. Phase 2's proof was a
throwaway repository whose implement ticks wrote one note each; this is real
work on a real repository, and the run that performs it is the evidence.

One safety property worth stating: this deletes the packages `tk herd` runs on.
Because ticfac drives the run with its OWN herdr executor, the run never uses
the thing it is removing. Do NOT orchestrate this epic through `tk herd`.

Scope, from ticfac epic av8's retro (`.tick/logs/herd/av8/RETRO.md` in ticfac):

- The execution half of `internal/herd/**`: client, herdtest, gitcmd, spawn,
  wait, reconcile, cleanup, state, and whatever of notify/paint/collect moves
  with them. `relay` and `dashboard` STAY — relay is the durable operator
  question and is tracker domain; dashboard exists to join tracker state with
  run state and has no seam inside its types.
- `internal/factory/**`, `internal/gatewaytrace`, `cloud/factory`,
  `cloud/sandbox`, the factory and cloud commands in `cmd/tk`, and the
  module-root embeds those leave unused.
- NOT `internal/tkcontract` — `cmd/tk`'s own version and root contract gate use
  it.
- The ten direct `.tick/` reads the retired packages hold.

Plan the child ticks at the start of this epic, not now. Sequence matters: the
deletions are irreversible and `tk` must keep working at every step.

## Deviations from the scope above, accepted at review

Recorded here because the scope list is what the epic record asserts, and two
items on it were deliberately NOT deleted. Both were reviewed and accepted; the
record must not keep claiming otherwise.

- **`cloud/sandbox` stays.** `internal/sandbox` shells into its scripts to warm
  local worktrees, and `internal/sandbox` was never in delete scope. Kept for
  that reason; the reason had been recorded only in a comment in `embedded.go`,
  which is why close-out found it and nothing earlier did. Finishing the
  deletion or settling the record permanently is tick g69.
- **Six `tk cloud` D19 operator verbs stay** — branch, spawn, wait, collect,
  prbody, reconcile — documented in `cloud.go`'s own help text and accepted by
  the sx5 review. The scope line above says the cloud commands go; it should be
  read as the factory command surface, not these six.
notes:
2026-09-15 08:52 - EPIC RETRO — pwp, closed 2026-09-15. Written by the operator because the closeout role cannot commit its own deliverable (ticfac tick 54n): the boundary forbids a worker writing .tick/, and the retro lives there. Attempts 11-14 each did the thinking and filed it as findings instead.

## What the epic delivered

416 files changed, 4,361 insertions, 108,616 deletions. tk herd spawn/wait/collect/reconcile/cleanup/notify/paint/guard/plugin, the factory command surface and its cloud worker, and the execution state they carried are gone. dashboard and relay remain, as scoped.

The checklist was what must SURVIVE. Verified: tk builds and its tests pass, internal/tkcontract untouched, relay and dashboard still work, every removed command checked against its ticfac equivalent rather than trusted from the plan. CI is green on PR 87 across all seven jobs.

## What this run proved about ticfac

This was the production run Phase 3 asks for, and it is evidence in both directions.

It works: eight ticks, fourteen attempts, herdr workers on pi/GLM-5.3, durable evidence, integrated gates, finding triage, and a review that refused to pass a diff it had real concerns about. Nothing merged that the gate had not proven.

It is not finished: the run died three times from one defect (FETCH_HEAD is process-global, so an operator merely WATCHING the run corrupted its view — fixed in ticfac ea1baed and proven by the run surviving the same observation afterwards). Close-out cannot write its deliverable at all. Adoption takes the oldest surviving attempt rather than the newest, and did so here — the epic closed its review on attempt 9's report while attempt 10's, which found the CI blocker, was the better one. Eleven further defects are filed against Phase 3.

## Does 'extracted' now mean extracted?

Structurally yes; practically not yet, and the honest answer is the second one.

The orchestration surface is out of this repository and ticfac ran the removal itself. But the epic left TWO herdr clients here (tlq, four files byte-identical), cloud/sandbox survived its own delete list (g69), and ticfac has no install path at all — no release pipeline, no skill, reachable only by go build (ticfac epic 2jn). A user cannot act on 'it moved to ticfac' today. Until tlq and 2jn land, 'extracted' is true of the code and not yet true of the product.

## Known gaps, all tracked

ticks: tlq (two herdr clients), si0 (plugin hooks call deleted commands and fail silently), hbi (manifest readers with no writer), g69 (cloud/sandbox record), tyj + 0c0 (help text and wiki), l8l (pin the workflow's named packages), 71y (reference ticfac from the skill).
ticfac: glb, cwa, her, 0iz, 4ys, 54n, 48q, w1c, udp, ix9, wdb, e08, 2jn.

## Two repairs made inside this epic

338bbf8b removed ./internal/herd/collect from ci.yml's parity step — a package nkf deleted, which five green gates never saw because the gate runs 'go test ./...' and that compiles only what exists. And the public-repo guard was taught not to read a content digest as an account id, after ticfac's truncated-sha256 digest fields produced 60 false findings.
acceptance_criteria: internal/herd contains only relay and dashboard plus what they need; internal/factory, internal/gatewaytrace, cloud/factory and cloud/sandbox are gone along with the factory and cloud commands and the embeds they leave unused; internal/tkcontract is untouched; the ten direct .tick/ reads in the retired packages are gone; tk builds and its tests pass; the same commands work from the ticfac CLI; and this epic was RUN by ticfac against this repository, not by tk herd, with the run shown.
